sentences.text: The meeting discussed the architecture of the GUI for speaker characterization, data storage formats, and the design of a start-up screen.
Participants agreed on using object files for pre-processed data and decided to implement a start-up screen with search and browse options.
The group also scheduled a follow-up meeting for Friday at 3:00 PM to discuss further implementation details.
Participant A explained that the data processing for speaker characterization is currently fine but they do not want to build the GUI for it.
Participant C suggested that the data should be stored as object files rather than raw text, noting that the current hash tables contain speaker names and percentages.
Participant B proposed that the data structures should be modular, allowing different components to plug into a common architecture.
Participant A described the current data model where separate classes represent speakers and meetings, containing all necessary information within each object.
Participant C asked if the data had already been calculated and stored, to which Participant A confirmed it is pre-processed and stored as object files.
Participant C inquired about the method for populating the topic box, and Participant A explained it is currently populated by the speaker present.
Participant C discussed the need for a start-up screen, asking whether it should include general information about the project or specific meeting details.
Participant B suggested that the start-up screen could guide users to common tasks, such as searching or browsing specific meetings or speakers.
Participant B raised the issue of whether the search results should be ranked based on Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) scores.
Participant C argued that ranking would be useful to distinguish between meetings where a term is frequently used versus those where it is only mentioned briefly.
No formal decisions were reached regarding the ranking of search results or the specific layout of the start-up screen.
The group agreed to schedule a follow-up meeting for Friday at 3:00 PM.
Participant C will write up the meeting minutes and send them to Participant B (Pernilla).
Participant B will create a modified copy of the file with the necessary changes for loading the search functionality.
Participant A will continue working on the data processing and object loading methods.
